re_line: Solomon Islands scraps China security pact ahead of Australia treaty · Coalition rejects $500m Vanuatu pact over net zero clause · Wong warns US-China rivalry is making world more dangerous · Parliament passes contentious defence security zones bill · COP31 ends in deadlock, Pacific leaders voice frustration
morning_memo: Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale has told Beijing he will terminate the 2022 China security pact, clearing the way for a new treaty with Australia due to be signed in Canberra on Wednesday.

The Coalition's rejection of the $500 million Nakamal Agreement with Vanuatu over its net zero clause exposes a bipartisan fault line in Australia's Pacific strategy, even though the pact does not require parliamentary ratification.
Foreign Minister Penny Wong told parliament that US-China rivalry is making the world more dangerous, reaffirming the US alliance while warning against nostalgia for a world that no longer exists.

top_stories.headline: Solomon Islands scraps China security pact ahead of Australia treaty signing
top_stories.body: Solomon Islands has informed Beijing it will terminate the 2022 security pact that let China rotate police training teams through the country, with *about two dozen* permanent Chinese police present at any time. Prime Minister **Matthew Wale** landed in Canberra on Tuesday ahead of Wednesday's signing of a new Australia-Solomon Islands Treaty covering security, health, education, justice, infrastructure and climate resilience. Former Australian high commissioner to the Solomons **Lachlan Strahan** said he was very happy to see the back of it.
top_stories.src_line: per ABC News (Stephen Dziedzic): "'Massive win' for Australia as Solomon Islands scraps China security deal" · also SMH

top_stories.headline: Coalition rejects $500 million Vanuatu pact over net zero clause
top_stories.body: The Coalition says it will not support the Nakamal Agreement with Vanuatu because it commits Australia to net zero emissions by 2050. The *$500 million* deal, signed by **Anthony Albanese** and Vanuatu Prime Minister **Jotham Napat**, underpins Canberra's strategy to keep China from gaining a military foothold in the Pacific. The government does not need parliamentary approval to ratify the pact, so the Coalition's opposition will not block it in the short term.
top_stories.src_line: per ABC News: "Coalition turns against security pact with Vanuatu over net zero clause"

top_stories.headline: Wong reaffirms US alliance, warns US-China rivalry is destabilising world order
top_stories.body: Foreign Minister **Penny Wong** used a major address to parliament to reaffirm Australia's alliance with the United States while calling for deeper partnerships with like-minded countries. She warned growing US-China rivalry is making the world more dangerous and urged Australia to move beyond nostalgia for a world that no longer exists. The speech came a day before **Anthony Albanese** finalises the Solomon Islands treaty and also flagged an Iran-linked AI operation targeting Australians.
top_stories.src_line: per ABC Politics: "Wong backs US alliance" · also ABC Politics

top_stories.headline: Parliament passes contentious defence security zones bill
top_stories.body: New laws letting Defence Minister **Richard Marles** declare temporary defence security zones and appoint defence security officials passed parliament with Coalition support, despite criticism from independents, unions and legal experts over possible overreach. The laws respond to concerns that bases are under-protected against drone incursions, with penalties of up to *seven years* in prison for trespass at zones such as the Woomera Prohibited Area and Pine Gap. Independent Senator **David Pocock** called the powers dangerous.
top_stories.src_line: per ABC News: "Drones, protests and new legal powers: what is in the new defence bill?" · also ABC Politics

overnight_items.headline: Bowen expresses regret over COP31 deadlock
overnight_items.body_text: Climate Change and Energy Minister **Chris Bowen** said he regrets COP31's failure to adopt a formal cover decision after the Antalya talks collapsed over fossil fuel language. Pacific leaders including Palau's **Surangel Whipps Jr.** had pressed oil-producing states for additional funding commitments to the Pacific Resilience Facility but left without an agreement on finance.

overnight_items.headline: Bloomberg: Australia pursuing another pact to counter China in Pacific
overnight_items.body_text: Bloomberg reports Canberra is working toward another agreement intended to limit Chinese influence in the Pacific, following the Solomon Islands treaty and the contested Vanuatu Nakamal Agreement. The report did not specify which partner state or what the pact would cover.

overnight_items.headline: Iran-based operation used ChatGPT to target Australians, Wong reveals
overnight_items.body_text: An Iran-based foreign influence operation used AI to create a fake journalist persona that posted about Australia's involvement in the US-Iran conflict, the ABC reported. **Penny Wong** cited the operation, disclosed by OpenAI, in parliament as an example of state actors using AI to destabilise and divide public opinion.

overnight_items.headline: Border Force seizes foreign vessel in largest illegal fishing bust
overnight_items.body_text: Australian Border Force intercepted a foreign vessel allegedly carrying more than *25 tonnes* of frozen fish in the Arafura Sea, following a pursuit that took officers into international waters. Authorities said the apprehension, involving commercial-scale gillnets and navigation equipment, could be the largest of its kind in Australian history.

pacific_wire.headline: Marshall Islands refuses to join COP31 consensus
pacific_wire.body_text: The Marshall Islands refused to join consensus on the adoption of the CMA text at the close of COP31, objecting to the finance and ambition levels in the final package. The move leaves the Antalya talks without a unified cover decision as Pacific states accused major emitters of backsliding.

pacific_wire.headline: Cook Islands weighs tuna fishery risks from deep-sea mining
pacific_wire.body_text: Environmental advocates in the Cook Islands say there is insufficient independent research to determine whether seabed mineral extraction can proceed without harming tuna stocks. Te Ipukarea Society director **Alanna Matamaru Smith** said the potential impact on tuna has become a particularly sensitive issue as the country explores a commercial seabed mining industry.

pacific_wire.headline: Niue Ocean Trust wins Earthshot Prize for ocean conservation model
pacific_wire.body_text: The Niue Ocean Wide Trust, founded by siblings **Coral** and **Brendon Pasisi**, won this year's Earthshot Prize in the Revive Our Oceans category. The trust leases Ocean Conservation Commitments for *250 New Zealand dollars* a year per square kilometre, placing all *320,000 square kilometres* of Niue's exclusive economic zone under sustainable management.

pacific_wire.headline: Clan chiefs sue Bougainville government to block Panguna mine
pacific_wire.body_text: Landowner clan chiefs have launched legal action against the Bougainville government seeking to block the redevelopment of the Panguna copper mine. The dispute comes weeks after Rio Tinto pledged to contribute toward impacts from its historic operation of the mine.

pacific_wire.headline: US lifts aid freeze for PNG, signals more funding ahead
pacific_wire.body_text: The United States has effectively lifted its foreign assistance pause in Papua New Guinea following USAID's integration into the State Department, US Charge d'Affaires **Alex M. Berenberg** said. He confirmed tens of millions of dollars in active 2026 funding and signalled millions more yet to be announced.

pacific_wire.headline: US proceeds with deep-sea mining lease auction off American Samoa
pacific_wire.body_text: The United States conducted its first deep-sea mining lease auction off American Samoa despite a federal judge having voided the environmental clearance for the sale. Community group Fa'asao Amerika Samoa said it will return to court to try to have the leases voided.

new_zealand.headline: New Zealand funds Tonga drought relief water tanks through MFAT
new_zealand.body_text: New Zealand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade is funding a Habitat for Humanity New Zealand partnership supplying water tanks to drought-hit households in Tonga's Ha'apai group. Live 'n Learn Tonga country director **'Alani Afu** said *47 households* received tanks in the first phase, with 120 more households to follow, as Tonga's 27-day state of emergency over the El Nino drought continues.

china_in_the_pacific.headline: Sogavare warns against scrapping China security pact
china_in_the_pacific.body_text: Opposition leader and former prime minister **Manasseh Sogavare** warned Prime Minister **Matthew Wale**'s GREAT coalition government against abandoning the 2022 security pact Sogavare signed with China, ahead of Wale's Wednesday signing of the new Australia-Solomon Islands Treaty. The sweeping Australia pact is expected to cover security, health, education, justice, infrastructure and climate resilience.

canberra_politics.headline: Labor seals deal with Greens on digital duty of care law
canberra_politics.body_text: Labor reached a deal with the Greens to pass digital duty of care legislation through the Senate, agreeing to amendments that increase penalties and give Australians a private right of action to sue social media companies for harm. Minister **Anika Wells** said the changes would make platforms more accountable, with fines reaching *5 percent* of global revenue for breaches.

canberra_politics.headline: Parliamentary inquiry recommends AI payment scheme for creators
canberra_politics.body_text: The Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence tabled a report with *46 recommendations*, including a new payment scheme compensating artists and copyright holders when their work trains AI models. The music industry rejected the premise that existing copyright protections are inadequate, while News Corp Australasia warned a voluntary scheme would amount to state-sanctioned theft.

canberra_politics.headline: Chalmers faces toughest moment as treasurer amid economic slowdown
canberra_politics.body_text: Treasurer **Jim Chalmers** is under pressure as unemployment rises and the economy slows ahead of the mid-year budget update, SMH reports. The piece argues Prime Minister **Anthony Albanese** cannot remove Chalmers despite the political strain, pointing to the lack of an obvious alternative and the risk of signalling instability.

canberra_politics.headline: Liberals and Greens unite as midwife protesters rally in Canberra
canberra_politics.body_text: Midwifery groups protested in Canberra on Tuesday following nationwide demonstrations over the weekend against the planned scrapping of a midwife insurance exemption. The protests drew an unusual cross-party alliance between Liberal and Greens parliamentarians against the government's position.

business_economy.headline: Major lender says RBA could cut rates early as economy weakens
business_economy.body_text: One of Australia's biggest lenders said the Reserve Bank could reduce the cash rate earlier than expected to protect a rapidly weakening economy. The forecast comes as Treasurer **Jim Chalmers** flags public service savings ahead of the mid-year budget update and unemployment climbs toward its highest level since 2021.

business_economy.headline: Queensland tungsten mine to double output for US Department of Defense
business_economy.body_text: The Mount Carbine mine west of Cairns, one of the largest tungsten deposits outside China, will double processing capacity to supply the US Department of Defense for fighter jets and submarines. Queensland Premier **David Crisafulli** said the expansion would create *100 direct jobs*, part of a broader US push to cut reliance on Chinese-sourced critical minerals ahead of a January 1 ban on Chinese materials for US defence contractors.

primary_documents.headline: Wong's full address: 'Securing Australia's future in a changing world'
primary_documents.body_text: The published text of **Penny Wong**'s parliamentary address outlining the government's foreign policy worldview, delivered the day before the Solomon Islands treaty signing. The speech urges Australia to shed nostalgia for a world that no longer exists as US-China competition reshapes the international order.
primary_documents.key_line: nostalgia for a world that no longer exists

primary_documents.headline: Australia issues joint statement on ICJ's Myanmar genocide ruling
primary_documents.body_text: Australia joined a joint statement responding to the International Court of Justice's finding that Myanmar is responsible for genocide against the Rohingya, a ruling issued on November 19, 2026. The judgment is final and binding, though enforcement falls to the UN Security Council.

calendar_watch.event: Signing of Australia-Solomon Islands Treaty in Canberra
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: The near-billion-dollar pact formalises Solomon Islands' pivot away from China after Honiara moves to scrap its 2022 security arrangement with Beijing.

calendar_watch.event: Final sitting week of the Australian Parliament for 2026
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: The digital duty of care bill, the AI inquiry report and the defence security zones law all moved through parliament in this closing week.

calendar_watch.event: US ban on Chinese-sourced critical minerals for defence contractors takes effect
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: The ban underpins the push for Australian suppliers such as the Mount Carbine tungsten mine to replace Chinese sources in the US defence supply chain.

calendar_watch.event: RBA cash rate cuts flagged by a major lender
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: An earlier-than-expected easing cycle would follow a weakening labour market and could shape the mid-year budget outlook Chalmers is preparing to release.

calendar_watch.event: Writs to be issued for PNG's 2027 National General Elections
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: PNG's Electoral Commission readiness, raised in parliament this week, will be tested against this statutory deadline.

key_stat.label: Value of Australia's Nakamal Agreement with Vanuatu
key_stat.context: The Coalition's refusal to back the pact over its net zero clause exposes a rift in Australia's Pacific strategy, even though ratification does not require parliamentary approval.

also_today.headline: World Bank economists trace why Tonga's resilience has not translated to jobs growth
also_today.body_text: Devpolicy carries a World Bank analysis by economists **Ruth Nikijuluw** and **Sebastian Stolorz** examining why remittances and resilience have not produced productive job growth in Tonga, tracing the missing links between demand and employment.

also_today.headline: ASPI: Australia overlooks scrap metal as a critical minerals resource
also_today.body_text: ASPI argues Australia's critical minerals and green steel push ignores scrap metal already above ground, much of which is still shipped offshore unprocessed, and calls for a domestic processing policy.

also_today.headline: Lowy: Australia's next critical mineral step is metallisation
also_today.body_text: The Interpreter argues that investing only in rare-earths refining risks missing the most valuable link in the critical minerals supply chain, metallisation, a step closer to the finished product.

also_today.headline: Lowy: Australia wants to regulate AI the way it tamed social media
also_today.body_text: The Interpreter writes that beneath great-power contest rhetoric, smaller democracies including Australia are steadily building leverage to set their own terms on AI regulation, drawing on the model of its social media laws.

also_today.headline: ASPI: Australia should security-vet employees of leading AI companies
also_today.body_text: ASPI warns that as companies and governments race to mitigate cyber vulnerabilities, they risk overlooking the trusted insider threat, citing recent cases involving Nvidia as a reason for Australia to vet AI company employees.
